record definition.subject: polymers and their reported properties
record definition.unit: a distinct polymer sample in one degradation test, or a distinct polymer sample when no degradation test is reported

polymer.additional prompts:
Always fill the 'Name' field using the reported polymer name, sample label, grade, or trade name; if the paper only reports an abbreviation such as PLA or PHBV, use that abbreviation as the name.
Return one record per distinct polymer sample and degradation test. If no degradation test is reported for a sample, return one record for that sample. Treat different comonomer compositions, blend ratios, molecular weight grades, filler loadings, and processing conditions as distinct samples.
Keep separate degradation tests for the same sample in separate records, even when they use the same medium. Keep the reported protocol, medium, temperature, pH, inoculum or enzyme, and other test conditions with their own results. Time points within one test belong to the same record.
During reconciliation, merge records only when both the sample identity and test context are compatible. A shared polymer name alone is not enough. Repeat sample properties across test records only when the paper supports that they describe the same sample.
If the paper is talking about a result from a previous paper, don't report that result.
Line notation rules. These apply to the 'Polymer SMILES', 'Monomer SMILES', 'BigSMILES', and 'Other structure identifier' fields:
- Only report a string that is printed as literal text in the paper, its tables, its figure captions, or its supporting information. Copy it character for character, including brackets, asterisks, dollar signs, angle brackets, and stereochemistry markers.
- Never write a structure string from your own chemical knowledge. Knowing the structure of a named polymer such as polyethylene, polystyrene, PET, or PLA is not evidence that this paper printed it.
- A drawn chemical structure, reaction scheme, or skeletal formula is not a line notation. Do not read a drawing and write it out as SMILES or BigSMILES.
- Never convert between notations. Do not turn a SMILES string into a BigSMILES string, do not turn a BigSMILES string into a SMILES string, and do not expand, canonicalize, or reformat a printed string.
- Do not repair, complete, or tidy a string that looks wrong or truncated. Copy it as printed.
- Most papers print no line notation at all. 'None' is the correct and expected answer for these fields, and reporting 'None' is never a failure.
Biodegradation rules:
- Only report degradation results that come from an experiment or an explicit claim in this paper. Do not report a material as biodegradable because polymers of its chemical class usually are.
- Use the end of the test as the common reporting time for scalar biodegradation and mass-loss results and 'Biodegradation test duration'. Do not substitute a maximum or a measurement from another time; if an endpoint value is not reported, use 'None'. Do not infer a missing duration from the test standard.
- Report percentage biodegradation, mass loss, and molecular weight loss in their own fields. Do not copy the same number into more than one of them.

Degree of crystallinity.prompt: Degree of crystallinity, usually from DSC or XRD

Tensile strength.prompt: Tensile strength or stress at break

Mass loss.prompt: Percentage mass loss or weight loss of the sample at the end of this degradation test, at the time in 'Biodegradation test duration'. Do not substitute the highest value or a value from another time. If no endpoint mass loss is reported, report None.

Molecular weight loss.prompt: Change in molecular weight during degradation, reported either as a percentage decrease or as the initial and final molecular weight. Include the measurement times and whether the values describe Mn or Mw; do not mix measurements from separate tests.

Degradation mechanism.prompt: Reported degradation mechanism, such as hydrolytic, enzymatic, oxidative, photodegradation, thermal, or microbial assimilation, including bulk or surface erosion when stated

Biodegradation certification.prompt: Compostability or biodegradability certification or label reported for this material, such as TUV OK compost INDUSTRIAL, TUV OK compost HOME, OK biodegradable SOIL or MARINE, BPI certified, DIN CERTCO, or the Seedling logo

Keep separate degradation tests for the same sample in separate records, even when they use the same medium. A different temperature, pH, medium, inoculum, enzyme, light condition, or chemical agent makes a separate test. Keep each test's conditions with its own results. Time points within one test belong to the same record.
Biotic and abiotic rules:
- Set 'Degradation pathway' from the experimental design: biotic when living organisms or their enzymes act on the polymer, abiotic when no organisms are involved, combined when both act together by design, such as outdoor exposure in soil, and abiotic control for a sterile, poisoned, or enzyme-free counterpart of a biotic test. Do not decide it from the name of the medium alone: compost also hydrolyses polymers, and a buffer can carry enzymes.
- Return each abiotic control as its own record, so the biotic and abiotic contributions stay separate.
- For a sequential test, such as UV ageing followed by soil burial, return one record per stage and describe the earlier stage in the 'Pre-treatment' field of the later one.
Endpoint and curve rules:
- 'Test duration' is the elapsed time at the end of this test. 'Mineralisation', 'Disintegration', and 'Mass loss' report the values at that time. Do not substitute a maximum or a value from another time; if an endpoint value is not reported, use 'None'. Do not infer a missing duration from the test standard.
- Preserve every reported time point in 'Mass loss curve' and 'Mineralisation curve', in time order and with units, including the final one. Use values stated in the text or in tables. When a curve is only plotted and you have only its caption, do not estimate values; name the figure in 'Mass loss figure' instead. When you are shown the figure itself, you may read approximate values from the plot, and must mark them as read from the figure.
- If the paper gives remaining mass rather than mass loss, label the curve values as remaining mass and do not convert them. Report 'Mass loss' only when the paper states the mass loss at the end of the test.
- Report mineralisation, disintegration, mass loss, and molecular weight change in their own fields. Do not copy the same number into more than one of them.
- Only report degradation results that come from an experiment or an explicit claim in this paper. Do not report a material as biodegradable because polymers of its chemical class usually are.
If the paper is talking about a result from a previous paper, don't report that result.
During reconciliation, merge records only when both the sample identity and test context are compatible. A shared polymer name alone is not enough. Repeat sample properties across test records only when the paper supports that they describe the same sample.

Test standard.prompt: Standard test method or protocol used for this test, such as ISO 14855, ISO 20200, ISO 16929, ISO 17556, ISO 14851, ISO 19679, ISO 4892, ASTM D5338, ASTM D5988, ASTM D6691, ASTM D6400, ASTM G154, OECD 301B, OECD 310, or EN 13432, copied exactly as named

Degradation medium.prompt: Medium or environment in contact with the sample, such as industrial compost, home compost, soil, seawater, marine sediment, freshwater, activated sludge, phosphate buffered saline, sodium hydroxide solution, simulated body fluid, air, or an outdoor exposure site

Test temperature.prompt: Temperature of this test, or its range or cycle when it is not constant

pH.prompt: pH of the medium at the start of the test, and as maintained or measured during it

Moisture or humidity.prompt: Moisture content or water holding capacity of a solid medium, or relative humidity of the surrounding air

Oxygen condition.prompt: Whether the test was aerobic or anaerobic, with how it was aerated or kept free of oxygen

Light exposure.prompt: Light exposure for photodegradation or weathering, including lamp type, wavelength range, irradiance, total radiant dose, light and dark or spray cycles, and chamber or outdoor site

Chemical agent.prompt: Chemical agent driving abiotic degradation and its concentration, such as sodium hydroxide, hydrochloric acid, phosphate buffer, hydrogen peroxide, Fenton reagent, or ozone

Agitation and medium renewal.prompt: Shaking or stirring rate, flow, and whether and how often the medium, buffer, or enzyme solution was replaced

Sample loading.prompt: Amount of polymer relative to the medium, such as sample mass and medium mass or volume, mg of polymer per g of compost or soil, or mg/L
Sample loading.example: <sample mass> g of <specimen form> in <medium mass> g of <medium>

Inoculum or microorganisms.prompt: Inoculum, microbial strains, or consortia used in or identified by this test, with their source and concentration or activity when reported, such as activated sludge from a municipal plant at 30 mg/L suspended solids, or Pseudomonas sp. strain

Enzyme.prompt: Enzyme used in this test, with its source or supplier, concentration, activity, and buffer, such as proteinase K from Tritirachium album at 0.2 mg/mL in Tris-HCl buffer

Controls.prompt: Reference materials, blanks, and sterile or abiotic controls run alongside this test, with their results when reported, such as a cellulose reference reaching 85% biodegradation or a sterile control showing 2% mass loss
Controls.example: <reference or control material>, <its result> at <time> d

Test duration.prompt: Elapsed time at the end of this test. Every endpoint value in this record refers to this time. Do not infer the duration from the test standard; if it is not reported, report None.

Mineralisation.prompt: Percentage biodegradation at the end of this test measured as carbon conversion, such as CO2 evolution, oxygen demand, biogas, or dissolved organic carbon removal, at the time in 'Test duration'. Do not substitute mass loss, disintegration, or molecular weight loss.

Mineralisation curve.prompt: Every reported time point of carbon-conversion biodegradation for this test, in time order, as value at time, with the measurement method, such as CO2 evolution, oxygen demand, or biogas

Biogas or methane yield.prompt: Biogas or methane produced in an anaerobic test, with units and time, such as mL CH4 per g of volatile solids after 60 d

Disintegration.prompt: Degree of disintegration at the end of this test, such as the fraction no longer retained on a 2 mm sieve under ISO 20200 or ISO 16929, at the time in 'Test duration'

Mass loss.prompt: Percentage mass loss or weight loss of the sample at the end of this test, at the time in 'Test duration'. Do not substitute the highest value or a value from another time, and do not convert a remaining mass. If no endpoint mass loss is reported, report None.

Mass loss curve.prompt: Every reported time point of mass loss or remaining mass for this test, in time order, as value at time, stating whether the values are mass loss or remaining mass and whether they come from the text or a table
Mass loss curve.example: <value>% at <time> d, <value>% at <time> d, <value>% at <time> d (mass loss, Table <n>)

Mass loss figure.prompt: Figure in which mass loss or remaining mass for this test is plotted against time, such as Figure 4a, identified from its number and caption. Report it even when the plotted values are not given in the text, so the curve can be digitised later.

Mass loss method.prompt: How mass loss was measured, including specimen recovery, washing, drying conditions, and the number of replicates
Mass loss method.example: <recovery>, <washing>, dried at <temperature> C to constant mass, <replicates>

Molecular weight change.prompt: Change in Mn or Mw during this test, as the reported values over time or a percentage decrease, with the time points and measurement method
Molecular weight change.example: Mn fell from <value> to <value> g/mol after <time> d (<method>)

Mechanical property retention.prompt: Change in tensile strength, elongation at break, modulus, or another mechanical property during this test, with time points

Crystallinity change.prompt: Change in crystallinity or thermal transitions during this test, with time points and method
Crystallinity change.example: Crystallinity rose from <value>% to <value>% after <time> d (<method>)

Chemical changes.prompt: Spectroscopic or chemical changes during this test, such as carbonyl, hydroxyl, or vinyl index from FTIR, NMR or XPS changes, end-group titration, or yellowness index, with values and time points

Surface and morphology changes.prompt: Surface erosion, cracks, pits, fragmentation, roughness, contact angle, discolouration, or biofilm seen during this test by SEM, AFM, or optical inspection, with time points

Water uptake.prompt: Water absorption or swelling of the sample during this test, with time points

Degradation products.prompt: Degradation products, released monomers or oligomers, microplastic or nanoplastic fragments, and the analytical method, such as lactic acid by HPLC

Ecotoxicity.prompt: Ecotoxicity of the degraded residue, medium, or products, such as plant germination, earthworm, Daphnia, or Vibrio fischeri tests, with results

Kinetic parameters.prompt: Reported rate constant, half-life, lag phase, or time to a stated extent of degradation, with the fitted model and units, such as a first-order rate constant of 0.035 per day

Degradation mechanism.prompt: Degradation mechanism as reported, such as hydrolytic, enzymatic, oxidative, photo-oxidative, thermal, or microbial assimilation, including bulk or surface erosion and random or chain-end scission when stated

Biodegradability statement.prompt: What the paper itself states about the biodegradability, compostability, or environmental persistence of this sample under the reported conditions, using the paper's own wording

record definition.subject: materials with reported electronic band gaps
record definition.unit: a distinct material, sample, composition, phase, or structure

band_gap_validation.additional prompts:
Return one record per distinct material, sample, composition, phase, or structure that is a subject of this paper. Put all reported gap values for the same material into that material's record. Treat genuinely different compositions, phases, structures, or experimentally distinct samples as separate records when their reported gaps differ. Do not split one material into separate records merely because the paper reports several calculation models, experimental methods, gap types, or conditions; preserve those distinctions in the gap items within the same material record. Do not create standalone records for materials mentioned only as general background or only in the reference list.

Evidence classification:
- A value belongs in 'All band gaps' only when the authors report it as a result produced in this paper, whether experimental or computational. Include results in the main text, tables, figures, captions, and supporting information.
- A value belongs in 'Cited literature band gaps' when it is explicitly attributed to another publication, prior work, a literature survey, or a pre-existing external database and applies to the material represented by this record. Do not mix cited values into this-study fields.
- Background claims without a numeric band-gap value are not gap records. Do not report activation energies, defect transition levels, formation energies, energy-level offsets, or spectral peak energies as band gaps unless the paper explicitly identifies them as a band gap, optical gap, fundamental gap, direct gap, or indirect gap.
- Never calculate a gap by subtracting band-edge energies, estimating a plot, or applying domain knowledge. Preserve reported precision, inequalities, approximations, ranges, and units.

Record formatting:
- For every populated gap field, return a JSON list even when it contains only one item. Each list item must be an object with exactly these keys: 'value', 'method_or_source', 'gap_type', and 'conditions'. Set an unsupported item component to the general missing value 'None'; do not omit keys or invent context.
- 'method_or_source': Report how the band gap was determined. For experimental values, include the measurement technique and extraction procedure where stated, e.g. 'UV–vis diffuse reflectance; Tauc plot' or 'absorption spectroscopy; absorption onset'. For computational values, include the calculation method, exchange–correlation functional, and explicitly reported corrections, e.g. 'DFT; HSE06; SOC'. For cited values, also include the reference identifier where available. Include only details explicitly reported in the paper.
- 'gap_type': Describe only the nature of the gap: 'optical', 'direct', 'indirect', or 'fundamental', including combinations such as 'direct optical' or 'indirect fundamental' when explicitly supported. Do not include measurement techniques, computational methods, citation information, or conditions. Do not infer the gap type from the method.
- 'conditions': Include only explicitly reported experimental measurement conditions, such as temperature, pressure, or atmosphere. Use 'None' for computational values or when experimental conditions are unreported. Do not include computational settings or sample synthesis conditions.
- A reported range is one item. Keep separate direct, indirect, optical, fundamental, phase-specific, method-specific, or experimental and computational values as separate list items. Deduplicate a value repeated without a changed context.
- Follow the general missing-value rule for unsupported fields. Return [] for the whole response when the paper contains no relevant band-gap materials.
- Use plain-text chemical formulae as printed. Do not add Markdown bullets, numbering, or newline-delimited pseudo-lists inside strings.

Material system.prompt: Specific material, sample, composition, phase, or structure represented by this record, including a reported sample label where available

Band gap.prompt: JSON list of the principal band-gap value or values produced in this paper for this material, including when only one value is reported. Each item must contain exactly 'value', 'method_or_source', 'gap_type', and 'conditions', following the shared rules in the additional prompts and using 'None' for unsupported components. Select values explicitly presented as principal or representative; do not choose solely by magnitude.

All band gaps.prompt: JSON list of every distinct experimental or computational band gap produced in this paper for this material, including when only one value is reported. Each item must contain exactly 'value', 'method_or_source', 'gap_type', and 'conditions', following the shared rules in the additional prompts and using 'None' for unsupported components. Preserve separate values determined by different methods, gap types, or experimental conditions. Exclude values attributed to prior work.

Cited literature band gaps.prompt: JSON list of every distinct numeric band gap for this material explicitly attributed to another publication, prior work, or an external database, including when only one value is reported. Each item must contain exactly 'value', 'method_or_source', 'gap_type', and 'conditions', following the shared rules in the additional prompts and using 'None' for unsupported components. Include the cited reference identifier in 'method_or_source' where available, alongside any reported measurement or computational method.
